chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a Muslim man who killed a Muslim man deliberately, and there were no guardians for the killed one from among the Muslims except guardians from the Ahl al-Dhimma (people under covenant) from his relatives. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is upon the Imam to present Islam to his relatives from his family. Whoever from them becomes a Muslim, he is his guardian; the killer is handed over to him. If he wishes, he kills him; if he wishes, he pardons him; and if he wishes, he takes the blood money (diyah).'

If no one becomes a Muslim, then the Imam is the guardian of his affairs. If he wishes, he kills him; and if he wishes, he takes the blood money, placing it in the treasury of the Muslims, because the crime of the killed one was upon the Imam; thus, his blood money becomes for the Imam of the Muslims.

I said, 'And if the Imam pardons him?' He said, 'He said: Rather, it is the right of all the Muslims, and it is upon the Imam to either kill him or take the blood money, and it is not for him to pardon.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: People under covenant (non-Muslims living under Islamic rule)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a Muslim kills another Muslim and the deceased has only non-Muslim relatives?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the mechanism of 'ta'wil' (interpretation) in inheritance of blood rights, where the Imam acts as the representative of the Muslim community in the absence of eligible Muslim heirs. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction that while the Imam can choose between execution, pardon, or blood money, his pardon is not absolute personal discretion but an act on behalf of the collective rights of the Muslims, hence he cannot simply waive the right without compensation. This ruling underscores the Imam's dual role as both a spiritual guide and a political-judicial authority in maintaining social order and justice.
